property_summary: In the reference C, owner() always equals the first immutable arg (creator); in the buggy M, owner() returns the collateral address instead, so calling collateral() and owner() on the same clone MUST return different addresses, but the bug makes them equal.

For any clone created by the factory, calling owner() returns the creator's address, which must differ from the collateral address returned by collateral(); the bug sets owner() to return the collateral address, making both equal.

For any clone created by the factory, owner() returns the creator address, which must differ from the collateral address returned by collateral(); the bug sets owner() to return the collateral address, making them equal.

For any clone created by the factory, owner() returns the creator address, which must differ from the collateral address returned by collateral(); the bug sets owner() to return the collateral address, making them equal.

For any clone deployed by the factory, owner() returns the factory owner (arg at offset 0x0) which must differ from collateral() (arg at offset 0x14); the bug makes owner() read offset 0x14 so it returns the same address as collateral(), making them equal.
The owner() function must return the address of the original CoolerFactory caller (owner), but the bug returns the debt token address instead.

The owner() getter must always return the same address as the 'owner' parameter that was originally encoded during clone deployment (i.e., _getArgAddress(0x0)), but the mutant returns the debt token address instead.
The owner() call must always return the address of the original deployer (encoded at offset 0x0), but the mutant incorrectly returns the debt token address (encoded at offset 0x28) for any clone.

For any clone deployed through generateCooler, the owner() getter must return the original caller (offset 0x0) and not the debt token address (offset 0x28); the bug causes owner() to return the debt address.
For any clone deployed via CoolerFactory.generateCooler, the public owner() getter must return the original caller/deployer address, but the mutant returns the debt token address instead.

The owner() function should return the address that created the Clone proxy, not the factory address; the bug makes owner() return the factory address, so for any given clone the returned owner differs from the true owner that holds privileged roles.

For any clone contract, the address returned by owner() must equal the address returned by the latest factory() call on that same clone, because the factory address is stored at a different immutable offset than the owner.

For any clone created by the factory, owner() must return the creator address (stored at offset 0x0) which differs from the factory address (stored at offset 0x3c); the bug causes owner() to incorrectly return the factory address, making owner() == factory() true for all clones, violating the invariant that owner and factory addresses are distinct.

For any clone created by the correct CoolerFactory, owner() must return the factory's msg.sender (the creator), but the bug makes it return the factory address itself, so owner() == factory() fails to distinguish them.

For any clone contract, the address returned by owner() must equal the first immutable argument stored at offset 0x0, which is the creator address passed by the factory; the bug makes owner() return the factory address stored at offset 0x3c instead, so owner() == factory() for all clones.
The collateral() function must return the address stored at immutable arg offset 0x14; the mutant reads from offset 0x15 and returns a different address.

For any admissible inputs, calling collateral() on the contract returns the address stored at immutable arg offset 0x14; the mutant reads from offset 0x15, thus returning a different address for at least one set of immutable args.

For any clone contract, calling collateral() returns the address stored at immutable arg offset 0x14; the mutant reads from 0x15, causing it to return a different address when the two offsets hold different values.

For any clone contract C created by CoolerFactory.generateCooler, calling collateral() returns the collateral token address stored at immutable arg offset 0x14; the mutant reads from offset 0x15, returning a different value when the sender address differs from the collateral address.

For any clone created by CoolerFactory, calling collateral() returns the address stored at immutable arg offset 0x14 (which is the collateral token address used during deployment); the mutant reads from offset 0x15, mixing the collateral and debt addresses, so when those two addresses differ, collateral() returns a different (incorrect) address.
The collateral() return value must equal the address packed at immutable offset 0x14, but the mutant returns the owner at offset 0x0 instead.

The collateral() address must equal the collateral token address encoded at offset 0x14, but the mutant returns the owner address at offset 0x0, so when the fuzzer deploys two instances with different owner and collateral addresses, their collateral() returns will differ in the mutant.

For any clone instance, the address returned by collateral() must equal the collateral token address derived from immutable args at offset 0x14, but the mutant returns the owner address from offset 0x0 instead, causing a mismatch when the two addresses differ.

For any clone instance, calling collateral() must return the ERC20 token address from offset 0x14 of the immutable args, not the owner address from offset 0x0, so the mutant returns owner instead of the correct collateral token when they differ.
For every deployed C clone, a call to collateral() must return an address different from the address returned by factory().
For any cloned C, the result of collateral() must match the address stored at offset 0x14 in the immutable args (the intended collateral token), not the address at offset 0x3c (the factory).
For any cloned C deployed by the factory, the ERC20 returned by collateral() must equal the original collateral token address used to generate the cooler.
